body:
Decided with the maintainer on 2026-09-28. Items on a checklist get an optional due date. It is
passive: nothing fires when it is reached; it only shows, and turns red once it is past. The
maintainer's rule for the UI: the date is a SIDENOTE, never the front of the row, and takes as
little space as possible.

## Wire (additive; PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 3)

* One more item field, `due`, in `fields` like the others: `{"value": "YYYY-MM-DD" | null,
  "updated_at", "updated_by"}` (a FieldClock of a nullable string). Field-level LWW like every
  field; absent = unchanged; null = no due date. Old clients ignore it and never overwrite it,
  since a push carries only the fields the client knows.
* Server: stored like `note` (columns `due`, `due_ts`, `due_by`; schema migration); validation:
  null or a calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD` that parses (no time, no zone), else `422 invalid_field`
  with `row_id`/`field`. Served on every item. Accepted on every list kind (the schema is one),
  the UI decides where to offer it. `docs/wire-contract.md`: the item field table, the validation
  rule, a sentence in "Protocol version" that this is additive.

## Clients (identical wording and behaviour)

* **Where offered:** the item dialog (add and edit) of a CHECKLIST only. Shopping lists and
  ledgers do not show the field; a due date already on an item stays stored and reappears if the
  list is switched back to a checklist (the hidden-field pattern of stores/price/quantity).
* **Entry:** a compact "Due" row in the dialog: the date, picked with the date picker the ledger's
  expense form uses (Android) / the native date input (web), and a clear action; empty by default.
* **Row display:** a short date in small muted text at the trailing edge of the item row, on the
  item's own line (beside the existing badges, before the edit affordance), never a line of its
  own and never wrapping the name (the name truncates first if the row is narrow). Short format in
  the user's language, without the year when it is the current year (Android AppFormat / web
  lib/format.ts get a `shortDate` helper; add cases to shared-test-cases if formatting is shared —
  it is not today, so keep each client's helper tested on its own with the same example dates).
  Colour is the only emphasis: the error colour when the date is before today (overdue), the
  primary colour when it is today, the muted colour otherwise. A checked item shows the date muted
  regardless. No bold, no larger text, no icon.
* **No reordering.** Items stay in their category order; the date does not sort anything.
* **Overview:** unchanged in this pass.
* Strings (nine locales on each client, identical English): "Due" (the dialog field label; reuse
  an existing string if one says exactly that), "No due date" (the picker's clear action, if the
  picker needs a label), "Overdue" only as an accessibility description of the red date, "Due
  today" likewise. Nothing else.
* Android: `ItemEntity.due: LwwOptionalString`, schema 11 → 12 (add-column migration + test),
  DTO `ItemFieldsDto.due`, sync merge like `note`. Web: `contract.ts` Item.due, the sync store,
  ItemRow, ItemDialog.
* Tests: server (validation, LWW merge of the field, served on pull, migration), web and Android
  (dialog only on checklists, save/clear round-trip, row colour for past/today/future/checked,
  short-date format, the hidden-field survival across a kind switch).
title: Due dates on checklist items: optional, passive, a small muted date on the row that turns red when past (both clients + server)
